This maize plot is our main food for the year, so I must put fertilizer even if prices are high — I will buy a few bags of urea and NPK, maybe through the AIP coupon if I get one, and stretch it across the 1.36 hectares. I keep a little manure from our goats and chickens and I will spread that near the planting stations before the rains, and I will buy hybrid seed because the local seed does not give enough on this land when I intercrop with beans and pumpkins. I cannot irrigate here — we depend on the rains — and pesticides I only buy if fall armyworm attacks badly, otherwise I handpick them with the children. Myself and my husband and the older children will do most of the work, and I will only hire a few people for ridging and weeding when the weeds get ahead of me.
